successors.note: Sale of 30 March 1850 for 10,000 pounds (Osu page). The Danish page says the forts were 'incorporated into the British Gold Coast', but Cliopatria's British Gold Coast row starts in 1873 and the Dutch dossier books British coastal land before 1873 (1868 exchange) under british-colonial-empire, so this dossier uses the same slug. The Cliopatria British Colonial Empire shape holds no cell within 30 km of Accra in 1850, 1860 or 1868 (gazetteer, 2026-10-19), so the land 1850-1872 has no British polygon.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1659; the page has Carloff reach the Gold Coast in January 1658 and capture 'all Swedish forts' in February 1658 (the Swedish page names Carlsborg at Cape Coast and Christiansborg at Osu; Fort Witsen was 'ceded' in 1658 without a recipient). Two fort sites.

976 km2 (six cells: three at Cape Coast-Anomabu, 1.2-1.07 W and 5.2-5.3 N, and three between Teshie and Tema), right for 1659-1684 while the Danes held Fort Frederiksborg at Cape Coast (acquired December 1659 on the Danish page, built 1661 on the Frederiksborg page) and Christiansborg at Accra. The Cliopatria years run on to 1733, but the English bought the fort outright in 1685 and the Danish forts table gives 1685 as ceded; from 1685 the keyframe danish-gold-coast_1685 removes the Cape Coast cells. The infobox gives 'over 10,000 km2' of Danish influence with no year (ratio 0.1 to the shape), which is influence, not enclaves.

correction.text: the 1659 shape without the Cape Coast and Anomabu cells, for 1685-1733: 'The English bought the fort outright, so the Danes lost it through sale'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe that splits the Cliopatria 1659 shape (1659-1733) at the sale of Fort Frederiksborg to the English in 1685 ('pawned to the English' in 1679, 'the English bought the fort outright' in 1685; rebuilt as Fort Royal in 1699). Three cells remain on the Accra side until 1733. The earlier version of this dossier put this correction on the 1659 keyframe itself, which would have removed Cape Coast from 1659-1684 as well.

1,349 km2, 1734-1743: Fort Fredensborg 'was built in 1734' at Old Ningo (0.18 E, 5.74 N); the shape adds three cells at 0.1-0.24 E. The Fredensborg page names neither builder nor how the land was acquired.

718 km2, three cells (gazetteer: 0.13 W-0.24 E, 5.67-5.9 N, around Teshie, Tema and Ningo), right for 1744-1783 as drawn; no forts east of Accra existed yet (Fort Prinsensten at Keta and Fort Kongensten at Ada 1784, Fort Augustaborg at Teshie 1787, Danish page), so the eastern forts are added by the new keyframes danish-gold-coast_1784 and danish-gold-coast_1787 and by /ledger gains 1784 and 1787, not by a correction of this shape. The fall from 1,349 km2 (1734 shape, six cells) loses three cells between 0.08 W and 0.1 E; the Ningo cell with Fort Fredensborg stays. It is carried by a confidence-1 loss event in 1744 (Opoku Ware I page: Ashanti 'occupied Accra and the coastal towns to its east' after the Akyem conquest of 1742; the Akwamu page is silent on 1730-1750). 'Almost all Danish posts' were abandoned in 1817 except Christiansborg and by 1835 Fredensborg held 'only one man', but the claims were sold in 1850, so the shape is not reduced.

region.text: Fort Carlsborg (Cape Coast) and Fort Christiansborg (Osu)

ledger.note: 1658: Carloff seizes the Swedish forts on the Gold Coast for Denmark. 'February 1658: He captures all Swedish forts, with help from the Dutch at Axim and local leaders including Acrosan (Johan Classen) of Fetu.' The Swedish page dates the seizure of Carlsborg 27 January 1658.

region.text: Fort Carlsborg / Fort Frederiksborg at Cape Coast

ledger.note: 1659: Commander Schmidt abandons Fort Carlsborg and sells it and the Danish stations to the Dutch (Danish page; Classen then besieges and retakes Carlsborg, a siege the page dates 1660, and hands it to the Swedish Africa Company on 10 December 1660). The Dutch page's fort table shows no Dutch occupation of Cape Coast after 1652.

region.text: Fort Carlsborg / Fort Frederiksborg at Cape Coast

ledger.note: 1659: the Danes get Fort Frederiksborg at Cape Coast. 'December 1659: A Danish West India Company expedition acquires Fort Frederiksborg from the King of Fetu.' The Frederiksborg page: 'It was built in 1661, with the approval of the King of Fetu' on Amanfro Hill.

1660: Fort Christiansborg passes to the Dutch. Osu Castle page, re-read 2026-10-19: 'In 1660, control passed to the Netherlands but it was soon lost to Denmark-Norway' (no month or day; infobox 'Occupants: Denmark-Norway (1660)'). Other pages put the Dutch earlier: the Danish page has Schmidt selling Carlsborg 'and all Danish stations to the Dutch' in 1659, and the Swedish page's infobox gives 'Partial Dutch occupation: Mar 1659 - Dec 1660' without naming forts; 1660 is kept because only the Osu page names Christiansborg. The Swedish page's 'On 20 April 1663, the capital Fort Carlsborg and Fort Christiansborg were again seized by the Dutch' (infobox 22 April 1663) is a second Dutch episode that the Osu and Danish pages do not mention; it is not drawn, and the Swedish page is silent on what followed.

1661: Christiansborg is Danish again. The Osu page gives no year for the return ('it was soon lost to Denmark-Norway', no month or day); 1661 is its infobox build year ('Built: 1661'; 'A substantial fort was built by Denmark-Norway in the 1660s'). The Swedish page's Dutch occupation ends in December 1660, which fits a Danish Christiansborg by 1661, but that page does not name Christiansborg. The page is silent on the date, so this bridges a silence (confidence 1).

1679-80: a mutiny at Christiansborg and the sale to the Portuguese. 'A mutiny led by the fort's Greek assistant commander killed the commander. A Portuguese ship then agreed to buy the fort.' The fort 'was abandoned on 29 August 1682'.
1683: the Danes buy Christiansborg back. 'February 1683: Danish forces returned after buying the fort back from the Portuguese.'

region.text: Fort Carlsborg / Fort Frederiksborg at Cape Coast

ledger.note: 1685: the English buy Fort Frederiksborg outright ('The English bought the fort outright, so the Danes lost it through sale'; pawned to the English in 1679; the Danish forts table: ceded 1685). The English rebuilt it as Fort Royal in 1699.
1685: the Danish Gold Coast's capital moves from Fort Frederiksborg to Fort Christiansborg at Osu.
1693: the Akwamu seize Christiansborg. 'The Akwamu occupied the fort after overpowering its weakened occupants, who were disguised as merchants.'
1694: the Danes buy it back. 'Assameni, the Akwamu leader, sold the fort back to Denmark-Norway for 50 marks of gold but kept the keys.'

region.text: Fort Fredensborg at Old Ningo, 5 44 N 0 11 E

ledger.note: 1734: the Danes found Fort Fredensborg at Old Ningo. 'Built: 1734'; Danish page: 'Fort Fredensborg is founded at Old Ningo'. Neither page says from whom the land was had. Region fixed by fx-41: the gazetteer lacks 'Ningo', so the 12 km disc is given by the Fort Fredensborg page's infobox coordinates (5.74464 N, 0.18333 E).

region.text: the three cells of the 1734 shape that the 1744 shape no longer has (between 0.08 W and 0.1 E, 5.67-5.9 N, the Tema-Prampram stretch and its hinterland)

ledger.note: 1744: Cliopatria's Danish shape falls from 1,349 to 718 km2 (six cells to three); Fort Fredensborg's cell at Old Ningo stays. No page names the Danish or this loss. Opoku Ware I page: 'After the conquest of the Akyem states in 1742, the Dutch paid a regular stipend on trade goods to Ashanti'; 'In the process, the Ashanti occupied Accra and the coastal towns to its east' (the page dates only the Akyem conquest, to 1742, and does not mention the Danish, Ningo or Fort Fredensborg); 'By the 1740s, the Ashanti held control over the entire coast of Ghana'. The Akwamu page (re-read 2026-10-19) is silent on Accra and Ningo between 1730 and 1750 and on any Danish involvement. The year is the year the Cliopatria shape changes; the taker is the reading of the Opoku Ware I passage, so this bridges a silence (confidence 1). The Ashanti dossier carries no mirror gain.

region.text: Prinsensten at Keta and Kongensten at Ada

ledger.note: 1784: Forts Prinsensten (Keta) and Kongensten (Ada) are founded. 'Forts Prinsensten (Keta) and Kongensten (Ada) are founded' in 1784; Fort Augustaborg at Teshie follows in 1787. The new keyframe danish-gold-coast_1784 draws the two forts from this year. Region fixed by fx-41: the gazetteer lacks 'Keta', so the Keta disc is given by the infobox coordinates of the Keta Municipal District page (capital Keta; 5.9031 N, 0.9868 E); Ada resolves as before.
1787: Fort Augustaborg is founded at Teshie. The new keyframe danish-gold-coast_1787 draws the three eastern forts from this year.

region.text: all Danish forts and settlements, including Christiansborg, Fredensborg, Prinsensten, Kongensten and Augustaborg

ledger.note: 1850: Denmark sells its Gold Coast to Britain. 'All Danish forts and settlements are sold to Britain and incorporated into the British Gold Coast' on 30 March 1850; 'In 1850, the British bought all of Denmark's Gold Coast possessions for 10,000 pounds' (Osu page); Fredensborg was handed over on 8 March 1850. The counterpart is british-colonial-empire, the slug the Dutch dossier uses for British coastal land before 1873; Cliopatria's British Gold Coast starts in 1873.

wars.name: Danish capture of the Swedish Gold Coast

union.text: Fort Carlsborg / Fort Frederiksborg at Cape Coast

wars.outcome: Carloff, with a Danish letter of marque of August 1657, sailed in December 1657, reached the Gold Coast in January 1658 and captured all the Swedish forts in February 1658; the Swedes demanded their return under the Treaty of Roskilde and the Treaty of Copenhagen (1660) gave Sweden 400,000 rixdollars.

wars.name: Dutch-Danish-Swedish contest for Carlsborg

zones.text: Fort Carlsborg / Fort Frederiksborg at Cape Coast

wars.outcome: Carlsborg changed hands several times: sold to the Dutch (1659), retaken by Classen of Fetu, handed to the Swedish Africa Company (10 December 1660), retaken by the Dutch (1663), taken by the English fleet under Holmes with Danish help (May 1664) and renamed Cape Coast Castle.
wars.note: The Swedish page puts the Dutch capture on 20 or 22 April 1663 and Holmes's seizure on 9 May 1664.

wars.name: Akwamu occupation of Christiansborg
wars.outcome: The Akwamu occupied the fort in 1693 and sold it back to Denmark-Norway in 1694 for 50 marks of gold, keeping the keys.

certainty.note: A few fort sites with undefined hinterlands: the pages give no boundary. The only sharp fact is the sale of 30 March 1850, which transfers the forts and settlements, not a line.

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW. 4 shapes, 1659-1852; all are three-to-six cell fort sites. Corrections: (a) new 1658 keyframe (Danish capture of the Swedish forts; Cliopatria starts 1659); (b) the Cape Coast-Anomabu cells run to 1733 but the English bought Fort Frederiksborg in 1685 (new keyframe 1685, the 1659 keyframe stays ok for 1659-1684); (c) the forts of 1784/1787 (Keta, Ada, Teshie) are missing (new keyframes 1784 and 1787; the 1744 keyframe is ok as drawn, so the forts are not drawn before they were founded); (d) the row runs to 1852 but the colony was sold on 30 March 1850. The 1744 contraction (six cells to three) is carried by a confidence-1 loss event to Ashanti (Opoku Ware I page; the Akwamu page is silent on the coast 1730-1750). AREA. Infobox: 'over 10,000 km2' of Danish influence with no year; 40,000 inhabitants in 1837. Cliopatria's shapes are 718-1,349 km2 (ratio 0.07-0.13). The infobox counts influence, not enclaves; the shapes are kept. DISAGREEMENTS. Start: infobox 1658, Danish page timeline February 1658, Swedish page 27 January 1658. Frederiksborg: acquired December 1659 (Danish page) or built 1661 (Frederiksborg page). Christiansborg 1660/61 (Osu page) vs Dutch seizure of April 1663 (Swedish page). Sale: 30 March 1850 (Danish page) vs Fredensborg handed over 8 March 1850. UNSETTLED. Fort Witsen at Takoradi was 'ceded' in 1658 (Swedish page) to an unnamed party and is Dutch from 1665 (Dutch page); 'Cong Heights' acquired from the King of Sabu in 1659 and taken by the Dutch in 1661 (Danish page) is not located; the 1817 abandonment of 'almost all Danish posts' except Christiansborg is not drawn because the claims were sold in 1850. The Danish 1792 abolition decree (effective 1803) has no territorial effect. The land passes to Britain 1850-1872 with no Cliopatria polygon; the counterpart slug is british-colonial-empire (as in the Dutch dossier), not british-gold-coast, which starts in 1873. COUNTERPARTS: Swedish Gold Coast (1650-1667), Fetu, Akwamu (af-04-x) need dossiers; the Ashanti dossier has no mirror of the 1744 loss. CHRISTIANSBORG 1659-1663: Osu page 1660 Dutch, 'soon' Danish, built 1661; Danish page 1659 sale of all stations; Swedish page Dutch occupation Mar 1659-Dec 1660 and a Dutch seizure of Carlsborg and Christiansborg on 20 April 1663 that no other page repeats; only the 1660 loss and the 1661 return are booked. REPAIR 2026-10-19: keyframes 1659/1744 no longer carry corrections that belong to later years; see _notes/af-04-a.md.
